key_insight: The study reports the first bulk synthesis of phase-pure Cs2AgBiI6, showing that removing trace moisture enables complete halide exchange from the bromide precursor.
engineering_relevance: This establishes a practical route to a stable, lead-free iodide double-perovskite absorber that can be made as both microcrystals and thin films for optoelectronic devices.
method: Start from phase-pure Cs2AgBiBr6 microcrystals or evaporated films
Perform anion exchange to convert bromide to iodide
Use dry/inert processing to suppress moisture-driven decomposition and preserve phase purity
evidence_signal: The resulting Cs2AgBiI6 shows a 1.70 ± 0.05 eV optical bandgap, near-IR photoluminescence at 1.03 eV, long-term room-temperature stability, and measurable photoconductivity in films.
watch_item: The synthesis is highly sensitive to trace moisture, so scalable processing will require tight humidity control to avoid incomplete exchange or phase impurity.
paper_title: Synthesis of the Elusive Bulk Iodide Double-Perovskite Semiconductor, Cs2AgBiI6: Microcrystals and Photoconductive Films
